take_homes: split on access, dialect or stance. otherwise one agent with a good prompt
give the synthesizer a framework (diagnosis, policy, actions) so it picks one answer and doesn't average
handoffs between agents are where work gets lost, and the audit checks the handoffs but not whether the answer is true

monday.move: run a three-retriever setup (confluence, docs, web) with a framework-driven synthesizer on a sales enablement question, then check the briefing's claims against the sources by hand
monday.who: me, plus one sales lead if they'll sit down for it
monday.stop_condition: stop if the briefing has a claim I can't trace to a source file, or if the sales lead doesn't care
monday.blocker: nobody in sales has asked for this, and I haven't worked out who maintains it once I lose interest

misconception.why: I skipped the review on the retriever outputs because they looked fine. Then the module said the audit never checks if the briefing is true, and I couldn't tell if mine was. I still think a good agent is mostly right, but 'looked fine' isn't evidence. I'm not calling checking a beginner thing yet.

one_line: a decent module on when to split, the framework trick was new to me. it would have been faster if it assumed you've already run agents.
